competitions.tagline: A comprehensive benchmark for systematic and transparent evaluation of post-hoc model explanations.
competitions.description: OpenXAI is a general-purpose library and benchmark designed to evaluate the quality of post-hoc attribute-based explanation methods. It features diverse datasets, pre-trained models, and 22 evaluation metrics across faithfulness, stability, and fairness. Users can benchmark their explanation methods and submit results to the public leaderboards.

participation.howToSubmit: Submit the performance of your explanation method for a given metric via the OpenXAI website submission portal.
participation.submissionFormat: Numerical scores for the evaluation metrics on the benchmark datasets.

competitions.quickstart:
from openxai.dataloader import ReturnLoaders
from openxai import LoadModel, Explainer, Evaluator
trainloader, testloader = ReturnLoaders(data_name='german', download=True)
model = LoadModel(data_name='german', ml_model='ann', pretrained=True)
exp_method = Explainer(method='lime', model=model)
inputs, labels = next(iter(testloader))
explanations = exp_method.get_explanations(inputs)
metric_evaluator = Evaluator(model, metric='PGI')
score = metric_evaluator.evaluate(inputs=inputs, explanations=explanations)

problems.name: Feature Agreement (FA)
problems.description: Computes the fraction of top-K features that are common between a given post hoc explanation and the corresponding ground truth explanation.

problems.name: Rank Agreement (RA)
problems.description: Measures the fraction of top-K features that are not only common between a given post hoc explanation and the corresponding ground truth explanation, but also have the same position in the respective rank orders.

problems.name: Sign Agreement (SA)
problems.description: Computes the fraction of top-K features that are not only common between a given post hoc explanation and the corresponding ground truth explanation, but also share the same sign (direction of contribution) in both the explanations.

problems.name: Signed Rank Agreement (SRA)
problems.description: Computes the fraction of top-K features that are not only common between a given post hoc explanation and the corresponding ground truth explanation, but also share the same feature attribution sign (direction of contribution) and position (rank) in both the explanations.

problems.name: Rank Correlation (RC)
problems.description: Computes the Spearman's rank correlation coefficient to measure the agreement between feature rankings provided by a given post hoc explanation and the corresponding ground truth explanation.

problems.name: Pairwise Rank Agreement (PRA)
problems.description: Computes the fraction of feature pairs for which the relative ordering is the same between the two explanations.

problems.name: Prediction Gap on Important feature perturbation (PGI)
problems.description: Measures the difference in prediction probability that results from perturbing the features deemed as influential by a given post hoc explanation.

problems.name: Prediction Gap on Unimportant feature perturbation (PGU)
problems.description: Measures the difference in prediction probability that results from perturbing the features deemed as unimportant by a given post hoc explanation.

problems.name: Relative Input Stability (RIS)
problems.description: Measures the maximum change in explanation relative to changes in the inputs.

problems.name: Relative Representation Stability (RRS)
problems.description: Measures the maximum change in explanation relative to changes in the internal representation learned by the model.

problems.description: Measures the maximum change in explanation relative to changes in output prediction probabilities.

competitions.name: LeanEval
competitions.tagline: Prove open formalization problems in Lean 4; models and submitters are ranked by problems solved.
competitions.description: LeanEval is the Lean FRO's comparator-based benchmark for formal mathematics. Trusted theorem statements live in leanprover/lean-eval; a problem counts as solved when the comparator accepts a submitted proof. Results are sticky per (user, model, problem) and published at lean-lang.org/eval. 301 visible problems, 71 models, 56 submitters, 71 active problems still unsolved.

participation.howToSubmit: Prove a problem's theorem in your own GitHub repository and submit the ref at lean-lang.org/eval/submit; the comparator verifies the proof and the result is appended to results/<login>.json in leanprover/lean-eval-submissions.
participation.submissionFormat: GitHub repo + ref containing the completed Lean proof, plus the declared model label used to produce it.
participation.computeDetails: Scoring is a comparator check of the proof; whatever compute the prover needs is on the submitter's side.
participation.eligibility: Open to everyone. Successes are sticky: an accepted (user, model, problem) tuple is never removed.
participation.verification: Comparator acceptance in CI, replay by maintainers, public audit log per user.

git clone https://github.com/leanprover/lean-eval && cd lean-eval
lake exe cache get && lake build
